title: Setup
lead: Every step below is required for the configuration this site runs — locale in the URL, remembered in a cookie between visits. Follow them in order and the last one puts a translated line on the page.
cli_title: Set up with the Svelte CLI
cli_lead: In an existing SvelteKit 3 project, one command does steps 1–5 below:
cli_then: It asks for your locales (the first one is the default) and whether the locale goes in the URL, then:
cli_messages: writes src/lib/messages/<locale>/common.json for every locale, with one greeting to translate;
cli_hooks: exports handle from src/hooks.server.ts, wrapping a handle you already have in sequence(), and, with the locale in the URL, reroute from src/hooks.ts;
cli_html: adds the lang and dir placeholders to the <html> tag in src/app.html.
cli_skip: Files you already have are left as they are. To skip the prompts, pass the answers inline:
cli_manual: Then render a message as in step 6. The sections below are the same setup done by hand.
requires_text: Requires Svelte 5 and, for this setup, SvelteKit 3. Without SvelteKit, import createDialect from svelte-dialect instead and skip the hooks: messages, t() and lazy namespaces work the same, while URL routing and server-side negotiation need Kit.
messages_text: One JSON file per locale and namespace, under src/lib/messages/<locale>/<namespace>.json. The value is MessageFormat 2; add a ru/common.json with the same key for a second language.
dialect_text: Once, in src/lib/i18n.ts. routing puts the locale in the URL; without it every export below still works, just against a cookie-only setup with no prefix.
handle_text: SvelteKit calls this on every request. It negotiates the locale — the URL prefix first, then the cookie, then Accept-Language — and writes it into the response as the page streams out.
reroute_text: Goes in src/hooks.ts — universal, not hooks.server.ts. Strips the prefix before SvelteKit matches routes, so /ru/about renders src/routes/about with no [locale] directory to add.
apphtml_text: handle fills these two placeholders as the page renders.
use_text: Import t anywhere. Start the dev server: the page reads “Hello, world!”, and /ru reads the Russian line once ru/common.json exists.
next_text: With that in place: write more {#messages}message files{/messages}, then read how {#routing}the URL prefix and the cookie{/routing} decide which locale a visitor sees.
